title: Parking Spot System
content:
Transformed the original parking slot system version 1 from CLI based to GUI through implementing Java Swing. Enabling users to search, display parking time, add or delete parking slots/cars.

Requirements:
- Clear representation of a parking slot system where users can search, add or delete slots and cars.
- To show comprehension in Objected Orientated Programming, advanced features are also added to develop visual hierarchy and prototypicality within the GUI.
- This included displaying parking times, time elapsed, removing and adding car directly from the slots.

To Start:
- Compile the application through 'Main' either on blueJ, console or any IDE.
- Selecting any of the displayed buttons to begin.
- Continue to explore the GUI and the advanced features implemented.

Have fun! 🙂

content:
⚡My first website portfolio after learning how to code for 6 months.

title: Rover Car Club of Australia
content:
Developed a revamped web application proposal for our client, RCCA who has hundreds of active users on their site. The new application allow users to upload and search rover related records with ease. In the admin dashboard there is an overview of database record, useful data analytics and a list of submitted files that are pending admin approval.

Technology Stack:
- Frontend: Astro, React.js, Tailwind & Mantine.
- Backend: Google Firebase & Firestore.

Features: 
- Upload of rover related records (eg. Journal Articles, Photograph Commercials, etc...).
- Search bar category filter for related records in database.
- Login and authentication for admin.
- Admin dashboard with overview of database record, data analytics and submitted files pending approval.

title: Socially - UNIHACK 23
content:
React Native app ran on Expo that was created for UNIHACK 2023: The Imagination Hackathon.
Link to UNIHACK Submission: https://devpost.com/software/socially-xe5619

✨ Inspiration
We wanted to help people in awkward situations become social butterflies! Especially as more people are struggling with social anxiety in post-COVID times.

⚡ What does the app do?
It's a mobile app that help individuals connect and conversate through suggesting ice-breaker style prompts (usually one or two sentences). No more awkward silences!

💬 Tell me more...
- When users are in a group situation and the conversation is dry, all it takes is a click of the button on their phone. Users can take charge of a conversation in real life and break out of their shell with the help of suggested prompts.
- Consist of a home page where users can search for topics.
- The trending topic page is a fun way for friends or even strangers to discuss about hot topics with a lot of media traction.  Isn't cold brew just dirt and water? Will Blackpink release new music in 2023? Is university degrees worth it?
- Jump into a hot trending topic with the conversation starters, it is so easy!

📲 How we built it...
Frontend/UI: React Native, Tailwind CSS, Native Wind & Adobe XD.
Backend: Django & SQLite.

⚠️ Challenges we ran into...
Integrating the API was challenging and was the last step in really completing our project well. We had to compromise and consider the time constraints. Although, we had built an active database (SQLite) on Django we still had to fall back on our dummy data as it was not integrating as smoothly as intended. Styling issues in React Native and creating the application as closely to our UI designs was also challenging. This is due to the restrictions with the push for Native Wind by React Native and its lack of styling freedom.

🏅 My Personal Accomplishments & Learnings
When I reflect back at this project, I am proud about how we collaborated together seamlessly and my overall leadership skills. This is the first time the four of us formed as a team and we achieved a solid MVP in less than two days. This is attributed to our unanimous decision to focus on the user experience and user stories. I also devoted a lot of my time to mentoring the other three members as they were from data analytics backgrounds and it was their first times using any of the technologies. I am proud at the technical skills everyone gained after the completion of the hackathon.

⏩ What is next for socially?
- We are aiming to make Socially highly customizable, allowing users to tailor the conversation prompts to their specific needs. Such as choose the tone of the prompts (funny, serious, thought-provoking, etc.), the level of difficulty, and even the length of the prompts. I guess you will have to be social to see what Socially will come up with next!
